newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Protest staged outside U.S. embassy in Bogota.
newsitem.headline: Protest staged outside U.S. embassy in Bogota.

text.p: Labour leaders staged a protest outside the U.S. embassy in Bogota Wednesday to protest Washington's decision to keep Colombia on a drugs backlist.

"Gringos get out of Colombia" and "cocaine users go home," were among the slogans chanted by the group of about 250 demonstrators, who blocked traffic on a main highway outside the fortress-like embassy compound late in the afternoon.
The demonstrators also burned U.S. flags while calling for a change in "interventionist" U.S. drug policy in Colombia.
"Frechette you rat get out," a reference to U.S. Ambassador Myles Frechette, was another favourite slogan.
About 50 riot police and soldiers, backed by four armoured personnel carriers, stood guard outside the compound.

Labour leaders, including the head of state oil workers union and Unitary Workers' Confederation (CUT) -- Colombia's largest labour group -- called for the demonstration to protest Washington's decision.

"We need international cooperation to get rid of the scourge of drugs, but this should be done with mutual respect," said Sen. Jorge Santos of the far-left Independent Revolutionary Workers Movement party.

"The people of Colombia have been harmed by this process of U.S. colonisation," he said, adding that President Ernesto Samper had "taken an attitude of submission and collaboration" in the face of U.S. intervention in Colombia's internal affairs.
"We're against this mechanism of certification," added Luis Eduardo Garzon, leader of the CUT. "It's just another way for the United States to pressure Colombia."
